classification.difficultyReason: Both compositions are explicitly requested and simplify directly by substituting the supplied linear expressions and cancelling inverse operations.

content.prompt:
Let $f(x)=2x+3$ and $g(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{2}$.

Show that $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions of each other by finding $f(g(x))$ and $g(f(x))$.

answer.short: $f(g(x))=x$ and $g(f(x))=x$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$. Hence $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=2\left(\frac{x-3}{2}\right)+3\\f(g(x))&=x-3+3\\f(g(x))&=x\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}g(f(x))&=\frac{(2x+3)-3}{2}\\g(f(x))&=\frac{2x}{2}\\g(f(x))&=x\end{align*}$$

Both compositions equal $x$ for every real $x$, so $f$ and $g$ are inverse functions.
